content.title: About
content.content: Whole wheat tortilla is a thin, flexible flatbread made from whole‑grain wheat flour, water, salt, and sometimes a small amount of vegetable oil. It has a mild nutty aroma, a sturdy texture, and a higher fiber content than white flour tortillas.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortillas originated in Mexico over 3,000 years ago and were originally made from corn; the whole‑wheat version became popular in the United States in the 1970s.
Whole‑grain flour retains the bran and germ, making the tortilla more nutritious than its white counterpart.
Tortillas freeze well and can be reheated in a microwave or on a skillet without losing quality.
In many cuisines they replace bread or flatbreads as a wrap for fillings.
Some whole‑wheat tortillas are labeled “gluten‑free” only when made with alternative grains; standard wheat tortillas contain gluten.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestive health and promoting satiety.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The tortilla delivers slow‑releasing glucose, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole wheat supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium, and zinc in the tortilla contribute to metabolic processes and immune support.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many baked goods, whole‑wheat tortillas contain minimal fat when no extra oil is added.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease should avoid whole‑wheat tortillas.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Whole‑wheat tortillas contain gluten and are not suitable for gluten‑free diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tortillas as the base for burritos, tacos, wraps, and sandwiches. Warm them on a dry skillet for a crisp edge or microwave briefly for flexibility. They pair well with vegetables, beans, lean proteins, cheese, and sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep tortillas in an airtight bag in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a separate bag; they can be reheated directly from frozen without losing pliability.
